record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.context_brief: Sublinear color changes on antipodal hypercube paths
record.original_question: For every red-blue coloring of the edges of the hypercube Q_n, does there exist a path between some pair of antipodal vertices whose number of color changes is o(n)?

evidence.quote: Question 8.2. Is it true that for every red-blue colouring of the edges of Qn, there exists a path between two antipodal vertices that changes colour o(n) times?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph, whose vertex set is $\{0,1\}^n$ and whose edges join pairs of vertices differing in exactly one coordinate. Two vertices $u,v\in\{0,1\}^n$ are called antipodal if they differ in every coordinate. Given an edge-coloring $c:E(Q_n)\to\{\text{red},\text{blue}\}$ and a path $P=e_1e_2\cdots e_k$ in $Q_n$, the number of color changes of $P$ is $|\{i:1\le i<k,\ c(e_i)\ne c(e_{i+1})\}|$.

Prove or disprove: for every $n\ge 1$ and every red-blue edge-coloring of $Q_n$, there exist antipodal vertices $u,v\in\{0,1\}^n$ and a path from $u$ to $v$ in $Q_n$ whose number of color changes is $o(n)$ as $n\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to be open. The best known result is by Dvořák (2020), giving an antipodal path with at most $0.375n+o(n)$ color changes in any 2-edge-coloring of $Q_n$, which is linear in $n$ and does not achieve the $o(n)$ bound asked for. No source found showing the $o(n)$ bound or a counterexample.

status_evidence.title: A note on Norine's antipodal-colouring conjecture (Dvořák)
status_evidence.snippet: Every 2-edge-coloring of Q_n contains an antipodal path with at most 0.375n + o(n) color changes.
status_evidence.claim: Best known upper bound on color changes is linear, 0.375n+o(n), not sublinear.

status_evidence.title: Antipodal monochromatic paths in hypercubes
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of Leader-Long type conjectures on antipodal paths with few color changes.
status_evidence.claim: The sublinear color-change question remains an active open problem.
